item.title: DA-Cordillera links Ifugao tomato farmers to Baguio buyers, offices
item.description: CHEAP TOMATOES. The Department of Agriculture - Cordillera uses Kadiwa trucks to bring fresh tomatoes from Ifugao’s farmers to various government offices, such as SSS, PIA, DepEd, and TESDA, as part of the marketing linkages of the agency during the produce’s peak production season. Sold at PHP20 per kg., the government agencies order from the DA their employees’ requests and the DA delivers them to the office. (PNA photos courtesy of Christian Rillorta, Liza T. item.title: PNP backs rejuvenated gov't anti-fake news drive
item.description: FIGHT VS. FAKE NEWS. Officials of the Presidential Communications Office and the country’s nine leading newspapers sign a memorandum of understanding on Wednesday (March 4, 2026) to combat misinformation and disinformation on digital platforms. The Philippine National Police on Thursday (March 5) committed its full resources to support the campaign. item.title: Globally recognized lifestyle hotel brand expands to Bacolod City
item.description: NEW HOTEL. PHINMA Hospitality officials led by chairperson and chief executive officer Jose Mari del Rosario broke ground for the TRYP by Wyndham Bacolod in a ceremony witnessed by Mayor Greg Gasataya Wednesday afternoon (March 4, 2026). The 150-room hotel will rise within Saludad, a 21-hectare masterplanned township of PHINMA Properties located along the Bacolod-Silay Access Road in Barangay Bata. item.title: CAVITEX Segment 3B seen reducing traffic volume by up to 50%
item.description: OPEN SOON. A map presented by the PEA Tollway Corp. during a media briefing on Thursday (March 5, 2026) shows the alignment of the CAVITEX C5 Link Expressway, highlighting Segment 3B (yellow), the portion set to open soon to connect existing sections of the expressway between CAVITEX and C5 Road. The new segment is expected to help ease traffic congestion and improve travel between Cavite and key areas in Metro Manila. item.title: DOH backs Bagong Balikbayan Act for health, psychosocial needs of OFWs
item.description: BACK HOME. Overseas Filipino worker (OFW) Rhodora Alcaraz safely returns to the Philippines on Dec. 16, 2025, after being hailed a hero for saving a three-month-old baby from a deadly fire in Hong Kong. Alcaraz was personally welcomed by President R. Marcos Jr., other government officials, and her siblings, upon her arrival to the country.
